item.description:

item.title: FREE CookieRun TCG Launch Event! — Fri Aug 14, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Durham Geeks **CookieRun** is the new Trading Card Game that has taken Asia by storm and has finally reached the states! What if Pokemon TCG was actually fun to play? That's what you'll be getting: a mechanically superior and actually affordable TCG that we are completely obsessed with at Guildhall Games!
**6:00pm - 7:00pm:** Learn to play **CookieRun**! We'll be having a class and one on one assistance in picking up the basics.

item.title: Mud Day (Raleigh) — Sat Aug 15, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Join NCWF South Wake Conservationists Chapter at Mud Day at the Walnut Creek Wetland Center! Stop by and participate in a variety of fun hands-on activities. This is always a fun event, and SWC is excited to participate for the fourth year in a row as an exhibitor. We will have a variety of displays and hands-on activities and are in need of some volunteers to help during the event. It is all pre-packaged, so just come and we’ll show you the ropes! Volunteer for a shift or stop by the booth — come get muddy! REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Wildlife Federation

item.title: Deep River – Canopy to Bottomland: A Boardwalk Adventure (High Point) — Sat Aug 15, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Join NCWF Triad Wild Chapter in partnership with the T. Gilbert Pearson Audubon Society for a guided birding hike at University Park! Starting from University Park, participants will travel from the ridgeline overlooking the West Fork of the Deep River down along one of High Point’s prized new boardwalk greenways to take in the riparian ecosystem. Travelling from among treetops to near-ground-level views, the Deep River features a host of bottomland residents including the pileated woodpecker, Carolina wren, and even a family of beavers at work! The 2.8-mile out-and-back hike will take the group to the Piedmont Environmental Center and its busy bird feeders as the turnaround point. We will return by sunset, when the beavers will hopefully be out with the birds! REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Wildlife Federation

item.title: Whistle Down Wind Feature Film Premiere — Sat Aug 15, 7:00 PM — The Carolina Theatre
item.description:
Durham-born writer/director Andie Morgenlander returns to Bull City for the world premiere of their debut feature film. The project, Whistle Down Wind, was shot in Western North Carolina through an ethical framework promoting holistic production culture. The story goes like this, “When a drunken teenage kiss propels Janie and Alex’s quirky friendship into a hidden love affair, the conservative ideologies of their Appalachian hometown force them to confront the truth about their sexualities — and the bitter future of their relationship.” This premiere, an OUTSouth Queer Film Festival event, celebrates North Carolina’s role as an epicenter of Southern, LGBT+ cinema, spotlighting actors and crew members who got their start in Durham! Whistle Down Wind is a collaboration between Raleigh-based production company Glassfire and Justice Film Collective.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Durham Ghost Walk — Sat Aug 15, 8:00 PM — Fate & Folklore
item.description:
Explore the spooky side of Durham’s history on this tour of the city’s most haunted locations. From the disgraced sons of tobacco giants who continue to roam their old factories, to tales of tragic accidents whose victims still haunt the site of their end, and murder victims who stubbornly cling to their possessions, Durham, NC, has a shadowy side to its history. Travel through the city with the assistance of a professional historian guide, while hearing about the city’s creepiest folklore.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Beginner Fused and Stained Glass Votives — Sun Aug 16, 2:00 PM — Fusion Gallery
item.description:
Learn the basics of Fused and Stained glass in this combination class series. In day one, students will create 4 small 2X4 inch fused glass panels. In day two, students will learn the tiffany method of copper foiling to solder the panels together to create a custom fused glass votive holder. Students will leave with a finished project after the second session of this class. All materials are included in class pricing. No prior glass experience necessary. Please wear closed-toe shoes and bring something with sleeves.

item.title: Invasive Removal with ReWild NC (Knightdale) — Mon Aug 17, 3:00 PM
item.description:
Join NCWF South Wake Conservationists Chapter and ReWild NC for an invasive removal along Mingo Creek Trail in Knightdale! Volunteers will help remove privet from the floodplain along the creek. Continuing the invasive removal work along this trail helps improve access to Mingo Creek for all non-human creatures living nearby and makes it easier for humans to enjoy the woods along the trail as well (rather than simply facing a wall of privet). The project will be led by Steven Feurstein the founder of ReWild NC. This is both an educational and joyful experience to partner to remove invasive plants! REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Wildlife Federation

Join the Media and Democracy Project to better understand and respond to the factors that influence public opinion, voters and democracy. Each session we will activate on a current information-related subject to help Fix Media Now.

item.title: FEMMES+ Summer Camp Begins — Tue Aug 18 — None
item.description:
Every August, FEMMES+ holds a week-long summer day camp at Duke for over eighty 4th-6th grade students in Durham. Duke University's undergraduate students serve as both counselors and mentors. For example, the theme of FEMMES+ Summer Camp 2019 was Blast to the Past, and we incorporated fun hands-on activities such as crystal growing, lava lamps, tie dye, building an app, and Newton's cradle. The camp was a huge success, and we are excited to continue offering this opportunity to students in the RTP area for years to come.
FEMMES+ is open to all that support FEMMES+ mission, regardless of gender. All students are welcome to join. FEMMES+ adheres to and complies with Duke University's non-discrimination policy.
Source: Duke University

item.description:
Triangle Hiking and Outdoors Group We'll be starting near Southpoint and final starting point will be sent out Monday evening.
Make sure that your bike is in good working order - tires hold air and are up to pressure, brakes and shifters work and your chain has been oiled.

item.title: A History of Occoneechee Mountain - The Pinnacle of the Triangle (Hillsborough) — Sun Aug 23, 4:30 PM
item.description:
Join NCWF Tri-County Conservationists Chapter for a hike at Occoneechee Mountain State Natural Area. This 2.7-mile loop will take participants up to an overlook with views of an old quarry site, the Eno River, and the Town of Hillsborough. With the highest elevation in the Triangle, the history, both anthropological and natural, of this area is as rich as the minerals it is compiled of. This state natural area is named for the Occaneechi, a Native American tribe which calls this area home. The mountain here was partially turned into a quarry and was mined for pyrophillite and other minerals. This gem of a site boasts summer tanagers and vireos in tranquil woodland trails circling the mountain and is graced by goldfinch and woodpecker calls. Be it the rolling tree-covered hills with homes and businesses dotting the valley landscape or the slow-moving Eno River framed by rock formations, this is a place you will not want to miss! REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Wildlife Federation

item.title: *VIRTUAL* SF/F Group — Tue Sep 1, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Durham Writers Group **Zoom Info Below Description**
This sub-group focuses on Science Fiction and Fantasy, so if you have anything that falls under that category — be it short story, poem, novel-in-progress or screenplay — then come! We'd love to hear from you.
Our format allows each reader 15 minutes to present their work... followed by approximately 20 minutes of feedback from the other attendees. To ensure a fair opportunity to respond, each attendee is limited to 1 minute of feedback time. (We usually get through three readers.)
If a reader elects to post their work in advance (NOT a requirement!), members will be able to access that work at our Google Group: https://groups.google.com/d/forum/durham-sff-writers-group
We ask all members to provide a warning, both on the Google Group and during the meeting, if their story features content that some readers might find upsetting. This includes descriptions of sexual violence.

item.title: Junior Ranger Discovery Hike — Sat Sep 26, 11:00 AM — Haw River State Park
item.description:
Calling all young explorers! On National Public Lands Day (9/26) and as part of Take A Child Outside Week (Sept 24-30), meet a park ranger at The Iron Ore Belt Access for a leisurely hike that mixes science, history, and conservation. Paticipants will be issued a junior ranger booklet at the trailhead and guidance for working through the activities with the goal of earning the park's junior ranger patch by the end of our adventure. Plan for a 1.5-2.0 mile, relatively-flat hike over natural surface trails, mostly shaded but with potential for some open, sunny areas. No two hikes are ever alike... What will you discover on our walk through the woods?
Please wear close-toed shoes, a hat or umbrella for sun protection if you like, and bring bottled water plus whatever you need to be comfortable for a two-hour nature walk.
